title: Dynamic pin escape and weighted canary resilience
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Long-lived model-version pins (session or shard affinity) can prevent safe traffic shifts during canary/A-B rollouts when capacity or variant availability changes. Currently pins either hold forever until TTL expires or are forcibly evicted, both of which cause undesirable user-visible flaps or increased error rates when the pinned variant becomes overloaded or degraded.

Goal: Implement a dynamic pin escape mechanism combined with a weighted-canary resilience policy so pinned sessions gradually and safely migrate away from unhealthy or low-capacity variants while preserving most-session affinity and minimizing user-level regressions. This should enable faster rollouts without global pin invalidation and provide clear observability and rollback controls for platform operators.

Scope: runtime route-resolver, session-store pin metadata, orchestrator signals (health/capacity), and console rollout controls. Non-goal: changing global semantics for permanent pin overrides (we keep strong affinity unless escape thresholds are met).
background: We've observed two recurring outage patterns in existing rollouts: 1) a canary variant runs out of cache/GPU memory due to uneven pin migration and causes elevated 5xx; 2) operators trying to accelerate rollouts manually revoke all pins which causes high churn and client-visible latency spikes. Existing tickets (see ENG-274501 and ENG-41827) explored pin reconciliation but left open a safe in-band migration policy. UX/design asked for a transparent migration window that can be tuned per release.
decisions: Represent pins as small differential metadata: {variant_id, pin_tier, created_at, last_served_at, escape_score}. Escape decisions are deterministic and local to route-resolver so no global coordination is required.

Introduce an escape_score that increases when: (a) variant reports health or capacity degradation; (b) request latency or error rate crosses thresholds; (c) variant is under a progressive drain due to rollout weight changes. Escape occurs when escape_score > escape_threshold OR when probabilistic escape trial is sampled.

Probabilistic pin escape: periodically (per-session TTL window) sample N% of pinned sessions for soft reassignment based on new rollout weights. Sampling rate is configurable per rollout and ramps up over rollout phases.

Weighted canary resilience: when fallback or overload is detected, the resolver uses a degrade matrix that prefers same-region higher-tier variants first, then cross-region compatible variants, minimizing cost-level escalation.
work_items: runtime: extend pin encoding in the request header and session-store to include escape_score and last_served_at (ENG runtime change)
resolver: implement escape scoring function and probabilistic sampler (deterministic RNG seeded by session id)
orchestrator: emit variant-level health/capacity signals and rollout-phase weight changes to runtime via existing pubsub channel
console: expose 'pin escape policy' controls in rollout modal (ramp %, trial window, escape threshold)
e2e: add synthetic workload tests that simulate hotspot pinning and confirm smooth migration without >5% error spike
docs: design short playbook for operators explaining when to increase sampling vs manual pin revocation
acceptance_criteria: Can enable dynamic pin escape for a single rollout and observe pinned-session migration in metrics without manual pin revocation
Pinned sessions are sampled and re-resolved according to configured ramp; sampling should be deterministic and reproducible in tests
A failing variant with capacity pressure triggers escape_score increases and results in >90% of newly sampled pins moving to healthy variants within configured trial window
No client-visible 5xx spike exceeding baseline + 5% during controlled canary migration test
Console shows per-rollout pin-escape rate and provides ability to pause/resume sampling
